newsitem.title: USA: US Senate panel sets ag research bill "mark-up".
newsitem.headline: US Senate panel sets ag research bill "mark-up".

text.p: U.S. spending on agricultural research would increase by $1 billion, or 20 percent, over five years under a bill to be considered by the Senate Agriculture Committtee, an aide said Monday.
The bill also would create a system for setting national priorities for research and would require more efficient use of funds, the aide to committee chairman Richard Lugar said.
Lugar, an Indiana Republican, announced a bill-drafting session for the committee on the issue of agricultural research for Wednesday at 9:30 a.m. EDT (1330 GMT).

Committee action would come one week after the Agriculture Department unveiled its proposals for updating its agricultural research work. At that point, Lugar said his committee and USDA were "moving in the same direction" of demanding that research have regional or national application and there should be more collaboration between researchers.

Both USDA and Lugar were interested in expanding the pool of institutions that could compete for funding. At present, the old-line land grant universities established under an 1862 law hold a dominant role in research.
USDA expends more than $1 billion a year on agricultural research.
In its package, USDA proposed a new competitive grant program totaling $200 million over four years to accelerate genome mapping of crop and livestock genes.
USDA also proposed keeping the $100-million-a-year Fund for Rural America alive for one or two years beyond its scheduled expiration in fiscal 1998.
Earlier this year, Lugar's staff circulated a discussion paper that suggested 25 percent of most ag research and extension funds would have to be spent on multi-state projects.
